AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: To evaluate whether cessation of renal colic is consistent with an expelled ureteral stone or whether imaging may be indicated even in the absence of symptoms.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: A retrospective study was performed of patients who presented to our institution with acute renal colic and ureteral stone and subsequently were evaluated at a follow-up visit where they reported complete cessation of pain for at least 72 hours.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Fifty-two (52) patients met inclusion criteria and reported no pain for at least 72 hours at the time of follow up visit. Fourteen patients (14/52 patients, 26% of total cohort) demonstrated a persistent ureteral stone despite denying any associated symptoms. Multivariate logistic regression did not show an association between stone size or stone location and the likelihood of passage in this cohort.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Cessation of pain was associated with passage of ureteral stone in nearly 75% of this study cohort, but 26% of patients still had persistent ureteral stones. We recommend routine follow up imaging in all patients with ureteral stones to document stone passage and avoid the risks of silent ureteral obstruction.
